question: Which Path 2 optimisation axis is the real bottleneck — replacing the phi ODE with elliprj, or NumPy-vectorising the per-epoch reconstruction loop?
hypothesis: The solve_ivp(phi_dot) call dominates Path 2 wall, so the elliprj replacement targeting it is the right next axis over vectorising the reconstruction loop.
narrative_md: cProfile of propagate_jacobi_path2 on the seed-89 truth state (5 warmed runs, 500 epochs): median 16.4 ms wall, of which solve_ivp(phi_dot) is 81% and the per-epoch reconstruction loop only ~11%. Verdict: the scipy.special.elliprj replacement (removes the ODE, vectorisable across candidates and times) is the right next axis; vectorising the reconstruction loop has too low a ceiling. Profiled on truth state -> oracle_clean false.
